title: Explicit banked-memory conjugate-orbit BSGS with charged routing and startup

claims.statement: For the full protected fixed-G1 pairing inversion problem, the banked conjugate-orbit algorithm in proof.md returns a valid G2 preimage with success exactly L/r>0.39, where m=39*2^121 and L=m*(2m-1). Total cold classical computation, summing all processors and charging every failed search, remote memory request, packet route, startup, preprocessing, pairing, output and verification, is at most 2^137 dense-Fp12 reference equivalents at fixed C=20000. Peak total memory is below 2^145 bytes, preprocessing below 2^137 equivalents is included, and nonuniform advice is zero bytes. No processor performs a load/store from a wide logical address; accesses are implemented by the explicit distributed-bank protocol. This is an analytical upper bound, not a practical production attack.
